worker.do-i-have-to-pay: Do I have to pay for an attorney?
worker.no-in-new-york-claimant: No. In New York, claimant-side workers' compensation attorneys are paid out of your award by the Workers' Compensation Board — never by you directly. The Board approves the attorney fee at the end of the case. You don't pay out of pocket and you don't pay if there's no recovery.
worker.what-is-an-ime-and: What is an IME and why is it so important?
worker.an-independent-medical-examination-is: An Independent Medical Examination is a one-time exam by a doctor chosen by the insurance carrier. The IME report is the single most common piece of evidence carriers use to challenge or reduce benefits. Showing up prepared — and on time — matters enormously. Missing an IME can suspend your benefits.
worker.how-is-my-weekly-benefit: How is my weekly benefit calculated?
worker.your-weekly-indemnity-rate-is: Your weekly indemnity rate is two-thirds of your Average Weekly Wage (AWW), capped at the statutory maximum for your date of injury. AWW is calculated under WCL §14 using your earnings in the year before the injury — multiple statutory methods may apply depending on your work pattern. Our free AWW calculator shows you the number.
worker.what-is-schedule-loss-of: What is Schedule Loss of Use (SLU)?
worker.slu-is-a-permanent-award: SLU is a permanent award for extremity injuries (arms, legs, hands, feet, eyes, ears, fingers, toes) under WCL §15(3). The award equals your weekly rate × the statutory weeks for that body part × the percentage of loss assigned to your injury. More on SLU here.
worker.what-if-the-carrier-denies: What if the carrier denies my claim?
worker.you-request-a-hearing-a: You request a hearing. A Workers' Compensation Law Judge (WCLJ) reviews the medical evidence, your testimony, and the carrier's defense, and decides whether to establish your claim. Having an attorney at that hearing materially changes the outcome — that's the moment representation matters most.
worker.no-attorney-matching-is-mechanical: No. Attorney matching is mechanical and neutral — round-robin by your county. We don't endorse, certify, or recommend specific attorneys. We're a software platform, not a law firm.

jsonld.what-is-the-average-weekly: What is the Average Weekly Wage (AWW) in NY workers' comp?
jsonld.your-aww-is-your-gross: Your AWW is your gross earnings for the 52 weeks before the injury converted to a weekly figure under WCL §14. Nearly every benefit in your case — weekly checks, SLU awards, LWEC classifications — is computed from two-thirds of it.
jsonld.which-wcl-14-method-applies: Which WCL §14 method applies to me?
jsonld.it-depends-on-your-work: It depends on your work pattern: the 260 multiplier for five-day workers and 300 for six-day workers who worked substantially the whole year, the 200 minimum multiplier for seasonal work, or a straight 52-week divisor. The calculator applies the statutory methods and shows each result.
jsonld.does-overtime-or-a-second: Does overtime or a second job count toward AWW?
jsonld.yes-aww-is-based-on: Yes — AWW is based on gross earnings including overtime. Wages from concurrent employment (a second job) may also be added under WCL §14(6) when the injury disables you from both jobs.

aww.gross-earnings-in-the-52: Gross earnings in the 52 weeks before accident
aww.14-subdivision-1-when-the: §14 Subdivision 1: When the claimant worked substantially the whole year, AWW = Total Earnings ÷ 52. This is the simplest method and applies to full-year, consistent employment.
aww.total-earnings-in-whatever-period: Total earnings in whatever period was worked
aww.straight-divisor-aww-total-earnings: Straight Divisor: AWW = Total Earnings ÷ Weeks Worked. Used by the Board when the §14 multiplier methods don't yield a fair result, or for irregular/seasonal workers, new hires, and part-year employment.
aww.hourly-quick-calc-aww-hourly: Hourly Quick Calc: AWW = Hourly Rate × Hours/Week. Useful when you know the claimant's hourly rate and regular schedule.

aww.weekly-earnings-at-2nd-job: Weekly earnings at 2nd job — added to primary AWW

aww.average-weekly-wage-aww-is: Average Weekly Wage (AWW) is the foundation of all New York workers' compensation benefits. Under Workers' Compensation Law §14, AWW determines the compensation rate — two-thirds (2/3) of AWW, capped at the statutory maximum set annually by DFS.
aww.14-1-52-week-divisor: §14(1) — 52-Week Divisor: For workers employed substantially the whole year, total gross earnings in the 52 weeks preceding the accident are divided by 52. This is the default method for full-time, full-year workers.
aww.14-2-day-based-multiplier: §14(2) — Day-Based Multiplier: When the claimant did NOT work substantially the whole year, average annual earnings are computed by multiplying the average daily wage by a statutory multiplier based on the claimant's regular work schedule:
aww.straight-divisor-board-discretion-when: Straight Divisor (Board Discretion): When the statutory multiplier methods do not yield a fair result — for instance, with seasonal workers, irregular schedules, new hires, or part-year employment — the Board may use a straight divisor: Total Earnings ÷ Actual Weeks Worked. This is the most commonly litigated AWW calculation.
aww.concurrent-employment-under-14-wages: Concurrent Employment: Under §14, wages from all concurrent employment at the time of injury are combined. If the claimant held two jobs, both sets of wages are included — even if only one employer's work caused the injury.
aww.why-it-matters-aww-directly: Why It Matters: AWW directly controls the comp rate, which flows into every benefit calculation: temporary total, reduced earnings, SLU awards, CCP awards, and fee applications. Getting the AWW right is the single most important number in the case.
aww.your-aww-is-your-gross: Your AWW is your gross earnings for the 52 weeks before the injury converted to a weekly figure under WCL §14. Nearly every benefit in your case — weekly checks capped at the statutory maximum rate, Schedule Loss of Use (SLU) awards, and LWEC classifications — is computed from two-thirds of it.

AWW calculations are based on current New York State Workers' Compensation Law §14 and Department of Financial Services regulations. The accuracy of results depends on the wages entered. Disputes over AWW may require detailed wage documentation and adjudication by the Workers' Compensation Board. Consult a qualified workers' compensation attorney for guidance on your specific case.

jsonld.what-does-lwec-mean-in: What does LWEC mean in workers' comp?
jsonld.lwec-stands-for-loss-of: LWEC stands for Loss of Wage Earning Capacity — the percentage by which a permanent injury reduces your ability to earn wages. The Workers' Compensation Board sets it at permanency (classification) based on medical impairment, functional limitations, and vocational factors such as age, education, and work history.
jsonld.how-many-weeks-of-lwec: How many weeks of LWEC benefits can I get in New York?
jsonld.wcl-15-3-w-caps: WCL §15(3)(w) caps benefit weeks by LWEC percentage — from 225 weeks at 15% or less up to 525 weeks at over 95%. Workers found permanently totally disabled receive lifetime benefits.
jsonld.how-is-the-weekly-lwec: How is the weekly LWEC rate calculated?
jsonld.the-weekly-classification-rate-equals: The weekly classification rate equals your LWEC percentage multiplied by your compensation rate (two-thirds of your average weekly wage, capped at the statutory maximum for your date of injury). For example, 50% LWEC with a $750 comp rate pays $375 per week.
jsonld.is-lwec-the-same-as: Is LWEC the same as a Schedule Loss of Use award?
jsonld.no-a-schedule-loss-of: No. A Schedule Loss of Use (SLU) award pays a fixed number of weeks for permanent loss of use of an extremity under WCL §15(3). LWEC compensates non-schedule permanent injuries — spine, head, and systemic conditions — with weekly benefits over a capped duration.
jsonld.what-attorney-fee-comes-out: What attorney fee comes out of an LWEC award?
jsonld.attorneys-are-typically-awarded-15: Attorneys are typically awarded 15 weeks multiplied by the weekly classification rate, deducted from the award and subject to Workers' Compensation Board approval under WCL §24.

lwec.what-is-lwec-loss-of: What Is LWEC (Loss of Wage Earning Capacity)?
lwec.loss-of-wage-earning-capacity: Loss of Wage Earning Capacity (LWEC) is New York's measure of how much a permanent, non-schedule injury reduces an injured worker's ability to earn wages. When a worker reaches maximum medical improvement with a permanent partial disability that isn't covered by the Schedule Loss of Use system — typically spine, head, and systemic injuries — the Workers' Compensation Board assigns an LWEC percentage based on medical impairment, functional limitations, and vocational factors such as age, education, and work history.
lwec.that-percentage-drives-both-the: That percentage drives both the weekly benefit rate and the maximum number of weeks the benefit is payable, using the bracket system shown below.
lwec.the-weekly-lwec-classification-rate: The weekly LWEC classification rate equals your LWEC percentage × your compensation rate (2/3 of your average weekly wage, capped at the statutory maximum rate for your date of injury). For example, a 50% LWEC classification with a $750/week comp rate yields $375/week.
lwec.the-duration-is-capped-by: The duration is capped by WCL §15(3)(w): the LWEC percentage falls into a bracket that sets the maximum weeks of benefits — from 225 weeks at 15% or less up to 525 weeks above 95%. Workers classified with a permanent total disability receive lifetime benefits.
lwec.not-sure-of-your-wage: Not sure of your wage figure? Establish it first with the Average Weekly Wage (AWW) calculator under WCL §14.
lwec.attorney-fee-is-assessed-as: Attorney fee is assessed as 15 weeks × the classification rate, deducted from the total award. For "Total (Industrial)" classifications, benefits continue for life.
lwec.lwec-vs-schedule-loss-of: LWEC vs. Schedule Loss of Use (SLU)
lwec.new-york-permanency-awards-come: New York permanency awards come in two forms. A Schedule Loss of Use (SLU) award pays a fixed number of weeks for permanent loss of use of an extremity — arm, hand, leg, foot, fingers, vision, or hearing — under WCL §15(3), even if you're back at work at full pay. LWEC covers non-schedule permanent injuries (spine, head, systemic conditions) with weekly benefits paid over a capped duration. A case generally resolves under one framework or the other for a given injury.
lwec.think-your-injury-may-be: Think your injury may be a schedule loss? Estimate the award with the free Schedule Loss of Use (SLU) calculator.
lwec.the-weekly-classification-rate-equals: The weekly classification rate equals your LWEC percentage multiplied by your compensation rate (two-thirds of your average weekly wage, capped at the statutory maximum for your date of injury). For example, 50% LWEC with a $750 comp rate pays $375 per week.
lwec.no-a-schedule-loss-of: No. A Schedule Loss of Use (SLU) award pays a fixed number of weeks for permanent loss of use of an extremity under WCL §15(3). LWEC compensates non-schedule permanent injuries — spine, head, and systemic conditions — with weekly benefits over a capped duration.
lwec.attorneys-are-typically-awarded-15: Attorneys are typically awarded 15 weeks multiplied by the weekly classification rate, deducted from the award and subject to Workers' Compensation Board approval under WCL §24. This calculator shows the full fee and net-to-claimant breakdown.

LWEC calculations are based on current New York State workers' compensation law and Department of Financial Services regulations. The classification percentage is determined by the Workers' Compensation Board and may vary based on medical evidence, vocational evaluation, and hearing outcomes. jsonld.what-is-radiculopathy-in-a: What is radiculopathy in a workers' comp case?
jsonld.radiculopathy-is-nerve-root-compression: Radiculopathy is nerve-root compression or irritation — usually in the neck or low back — causing radiating pain, numbness, or weakness into an arm or leg. In New York permanency evaluations it raises the severity ranking of a spine condition under the 2012 Impairment Guidelines.
jsonld.how-do-the-2012-guidelines: How do the 2012 Guidelines score radiculopathy?
jsonld.tables-s11-4-through-s11: Tables S11.4 through S11.7 assign points for imaging, EMG, motor, sensory, reflex, and tension-sign findings. The point total places the spine condition in a severity ranking, which feeds the Medical Impairment Class used at classification.
jsonld.does-the-severity-ranking-decide: Does the severity ranking decide my LWEC percentage?
jsonld.it-is-the-medical-impairment: It is the medical impairment input, but not the whole answer — the Loss of Wage Earning Capacity percentage also weighs functional limitations and vocational factors such as age, education, and work history.

radiculopathy.significant-disc-abnormalities-displacin: Significant disc abnormalities displacing nerve tissue and/or bony/mechanical nerve root encroachment on imaging, correlating with the clinical picture.
radiculopathy.fibrillation-potentials-and-or-positive: Fibrillation potentials and/or positive sharp waves in at least 2 muscles in the distribution of the involved nerve root(s).
radiculopathy.objective-muscle-weakness-scored-by: Objective muscle weakness scored by motor grade. Value from Table S11.4(a), capped by nerve root max from Table S11.5 or S11.6.
radiculopathy.grade-0-no-contraction-20: Grade 0 (no contraction) = 20  |  Grade 1 (slight contraction, no movement) = 20  |  Grade 2 (movement, gravity eliminated) = 18  |  Grade 3 (against gravity, no resistance) = 6  |  Grade 4–5 (against resistance / normal) = 0

radiculopathy.grade-1-slight-contraction-no: Grade 1 — Slight contraction, no movement (20 pts)
radiculopathy.unilateral-muscle-atrophy-shown-by: Unilateral muscle atrophy shown by bilateral circumferential measurements (calf, thigh, arm, or forearm) or inspection of hand/foot muscles. Difference ≥2 cm at matched bony landmarks is significant.
radiculopathy.reproducible-alteration-of-sensation-sha: Reproducible alteration of sensation (sharp/dull, light touch) consistent with specific dermatomal distribution. Capped by nerve root max from Table S11.5 or S11.6.
radiculopathy.deep-tendon-reflexes-biceps-triceps: Deep tendon reflexes (biceps, triceps, brachioradialis, patellar, ankle jerk) compared to the non-affected side. A difference of ≥1 grade is significant.
radiculopathy.0-absent-6-pts-present: 0 (Absent) = 6 pts  |  + (Present but diminished) = 4 pts  |  ++ or +++ (Normal/Increased) = 0 pts
radiculopathy.spurling-s-sign-cervical-straight: Spurling's Sign (cervical), Straight Leg Raise (L5/S1), or Femoral Stretch (L2–L4).
radiculopathy.the-severity-ranking-letter-is: The severity ranking letter is used with Table 11.1 (Non-Surgically Treated Soft Tissue Conditions) or Table 11.2 (Surgically Treated Spine Conditions) to place the claimant within the appropriate Medical Impairment Class. Per Table S11.4(b), for each additional root in the same spinal region, the severity ranking increases by one letter per level (max 3 letters).
radiculopathy.under-the-2012-nys-impairment: Under the 2012 NYS Impairment Guidelines, radiculopathy is scored using a point system defined in Table S11.4. Points are accumulated across six categories of objective clinical findings: imaging, EMG, muscle weakness, muscle atrophy, sensory involvement, reflex changes, and tension/compression signs. The total determines a severity ranking letter via Tables S11.7(a) or S11.7(b).
radiculopathy.six-categories-of-objective-findings: Six categories of objective findings, each scored Yes/No or by grade. Imaging (0 or 16), EMG (0 or 6), Muscle Weakness (0–20 per S11.4(a)), Atrophy (0 or 6), Sensory (0–6 per S11.4(b)), Reflexes (0–6), Tension Signs (0 or 4).

radiculopathy.maximum-point-values-for-sensory: Maximum point values for sensory deficit and weakness by specific nerve root. E.g., C5 allows max 0 sensory / 10 weakness; L4 allows max 4 sensory / 24 weakness. These cap the S11.4 scores.
radiculopathy.total-points-map-to-a: Total points map to a letter (C through H for cervical, D through J for lumbar). This letter determines placement within the Medical Impairment Class from Tables 11.1 or 11.2.
radiculopathy.per-table-s11-4-b: Per Table S11.4(b) note: for each additional nerve root in the same spinal region, the severity ranking is increased by one letter per level, up to a maximum of 3 letters.
radiculopathy.it-is-the-medical-impairment: It is the medical impairment input, but not the whole answer — the Loss of Wage Earning Capacity (LWEC) percentage also weighs functional limitations and vocational factors such as age, education, and work history.

jsonld.what-is-a-schedule-loss: What is a Schedule Loss of Use (SLU) award?
jsonld.an-slu-award-is-a: An SLU award is a statutory workers' compensation award under WCL §15(3) that compensates permanent loss of use of an extremity, vision, or hearing. The law assigns each body part a maximum number of weeks; your award equals your percentage loss of use multiplied by those weeks, multiplied by your weekly rate.
jsonld.is-an-slu-award-the: Is an SLU award the same as a settlement?
jsonld.many-injured-workers-call-their: Many injured workers call their SLU award a settlement, and the schedule of weeks by body part is often searched for as a settlement chart. Strictly, an SLU award is a statutory award driven by your percentage loss of use — different from a Section 32 settlement, which is a negotiated lump sum that closes the case.
jsonld.how-much-is-my-slu: How much is my SLU award worth?
jsonld.percentage-loss-of-use-the: Percentage loss of use × the body part's maximum weeks × your weekly rate (two-thirds of your average weekly wage, capped at the statutory maximum for your date of injury). Example: 20% loss of use of an arm equals 20% of 312 weeks, or 62.4 weeks; at an $800 rate that's a $49,920 award before deductions.
jsonld.can-i-get-an-slu: Can I get an SLU award if I'm back at work?
jsonld.yes-an-slu-award-compensates: Yes. An SLU award compensates the permanent loss of use itself, so it is payable even if you have returned to work at full pay with no lost time.
jsonld.what-is-deducted-from-an: What is deducted from an SLU award?
jsonld.prior-payments-made-in-the: Prior payments made in the case are deducted first, and the attorney fee — typically 15% of the moving (new money) amount, subject to Board approval — comes out of the remainder. The net to claimant is what remains.
jsonld.which-injuries-qualify-for-slu: Which injuries qualify for SLU instead of LWEC?
jsonld.slu-covers-extremities-and-sensory: SLU covers extremities and sensory loss: arm, hand, fingers, leg, foot, toes, vision, and hearing. Permanent injuries to the spine, head, or internal systems are compensated instead through a Loss of Wage Earning Capacity (LWEC) classification.

slu.schedule-loss-of-use-slu: Schedule Loss of Use (SLU) is a fixed benefit available to injured workers in New York State under Workers' Compensation Law §15(3). Unlike permanent partial disability benefits, SLU provides a predetermined number of weeks of benefits based on the specific body part injured and the degree of permanent loss of use.

slu.how-slu-works-the-law: How SLU Works: The law assigns a maximum number of weeks to each body part. slu.prior-weeks-paid-at-tt: Prior Weeks Paid at TT (PHP): Weeks paid at the temporary total rate during the healing period may be credited and added to the SLU calculation, depending on the body part schedule.

jsonld.how-are-workers-comp-settlements: How are workers' comp settlements calculated in New York?
jsonld.in-new-york-workers-compensation: In New York, workers' compensation settlements are calculated based on the type of case. For Schedule Loss of Use (SLU) awards under WCL §15(3), the value equals the percentage of loss times the number of weeks assigned to that body part, multiplied by the claimant's compensation rate (2/3 of average weekly wage, capped at the statutory maximum). Section 32 settlements involve a lump-sum payment that closes the case entirely and are negotiated based on the present value of future benefits.
jsonld.what-is-a-section-32: What is a Section 32 agreement in NYS workers' compensation?
jsonld.a-section-32-agreement-is: A Section 32 agreement is a voluntary settlement under Workers' Compensation Law §32 that allows the claimant and carrier to resolve the entire case with a lump-sum payment. Once approved by the Workers' Compensation Board, it closes the case permanently — including future medical benefits unless specifically excluded. Both parties must consent, and the Board reviews the agreement to ensure it is in the claimant's best interest.
jsonld.should-i-settle-my-workers: Should I settle my workers' comp case in New York?
jsonld.whether-to-settle-depends-on: Whether to settle depends on several factors: the severity and permanency of your injury, your current and future medical needs, your age and work capacity, and the strength of your legal position. A settlement provides a lump sum but closes your case permanently. An attorney can help you evaluate whether a settlement offer fairly compensates your injuries or whether continuing to receive weekly benefits and medical coverage is more advantageous.
jsonld.how-much-is-my-workers: How much is my workers' comp case worth in New York?
jsonld.the-value-of-a-nys: The value of a NYS workers' compensation case depends on your average weekly wage, the body parts injured, the percentage of permanent impairment, your date of injury (which determines the maximum rate), and whether you have a Schedule Loss of Use (extremity) or classification (non-schedule) case. Use our free calculator to estimate SLU values, or consult with an attorney for a comprehensive case valuation including Section 32 settlement potential.
jsonld.what-is-the-average-workers: What is the average workers' comp settlement in New York?
jsonld.average-workers-comp-settlements-in: Average workers' comp settlements in New York vary widely depending on the severity of the injury, the body part affected, and whether the claim involves Schedule Loss of Use or a classification injury. SLU settlements for a single extremity typically range from $10,000 to $150,000+ depending on the percentage of loss and the compensation rate at the time of injury. Section 32 settlements can be substantially higher or lower depending on negotiation and medical permanency findings. An experienced attorney can evaluate comparable cases to estimate your settlement value.
jsonld.how-long-does-a-workers: How long does a workers' comp settlement take in New York?
jsonld.the-timeline-for-a-workers: The timeline for a workers' comp settlement in New York depends on the case type. SLU awards are typically determined 1-3 years post-injury following maximum medical improvement (MMI). Section 32 settlements can take 6 months to several years to negotiate, depending on the complexity of the case, the strength of medical evidence, and the parties' positions. Once the settlement is signed and submitted to the Workers' Compensation Board, approval typically takes 1-2 weeks.

jsonld.what-is-an-independent-medical: What is an Independent Medical Examination (IME)?
jsonld.an-ime-is-a-medical: An IME is a medical examination arranged by the workers' compensation insurance carrier to assess your injury and level of disability. A doctor selected by the carrier — not your treating physician — examines you and reports to the Workers' Compensation Board. The IME doctor's findings can significantly affect your benefits, so it is important to be prepared and take the exam seriously.
jsonld.what-happens-if-i-miss: What happens if I miss my IME appointment?
jsonld.missing-an-ime-without-a: Missing an IME without a valid medical reason can have serious consequences. Your benefits may be suspended, your case may be delayed, or a judge may decide issues based largely on the IME doctor's findings. Always notify the carrier and your attorney immediately if you cannot attend, and provide documentation if possible.
jsonld.how-long-does-an-ime: How long does an IME typically take?
jsonld.most-imes-last-between-30: Most IMEs last between 30 minutes and 1.5 hours, depending on the complexity of the injury. The doctor takes your medical history, performs a physical examination, and may ask you to perform specific movements to assess your functional capacity. Allow extra time for check-in paperwork and travel.
jsonld.can-i-bring-an-attorney: Can I bring an attorney or support person to my IME?
jsonld.policies-vary-by-doctor-many: Policies vary by doctor. Many IME doctors do not allow an attorney in the exam room, but you may be able to bring a support person who waits in the reception area. Call ahead to ask about the doctor's policy. You are generally allowed to take notes about what occurs.

jsonld.what-travel-expenses-can-i: What travel expenses can I be reimbursed for in a workers' comp case?
jsonld.new-york-workers-compensation-reimburses: New York workers' compensation reimburses the necessary expenses of traveling to and from authorized treatment — subway and bus fares, taxis and rideshares, mileage in your own car, tolls, and parking. It also reimburses prescribed medicine and medical supplies you paid for out of pocket. Because the rule covers going to and from care, trips are counted round trip.

The Comp Desk fills it in from the trips and receipts you log.
jsonld.what-is-the-mileage-reimbursement: What is the mileage reimbursement rate for workers' comp travel?
jsonld.the-chair-of-the-workers: The Chair of the Workers' Compensation Board sets the mileage rate. It is effective-dated, so a trip is reimbursed at the rate in force on the date you traveled — for example 70.0 cents per mile in 2025 and 72.5 cents per mile in 2026. The Comp Desk applies the correct rate automatically based on each trip's date.
jsonld.do-i-need-to-keep: Do I need to keep my receipts?
jsonld.yes-keep-your-original-receipts: Yes — keep your original receipts for prescriptions, supplies, taxis, and rideshares. The Comp Desk lets you snap a photo or attach a PDF of each receipt so it is filed by date and ready to send with your C-257. Mileage in your own car does not need a receipt; it is calculated from the distance and the WCB rate.

privacy.in-short-calculator-inputs-are: In short: Calculator inputs are processed on your device and never sent to us. If you contact us, request an attorney referral, create an account, or opt in to reminders, we collect only what you provide and use it to deliver the service you asked for. Optional features like the personalized Road to Recovery and the Comp Buddy assistant use only information you choose to share, with your consent — and any research use of anonymized patterns is strictly opt-in and off by default. We do not sell your personal information, and we never share your phone number or SMS opt-in data with third parties for their marketing.
privacy.this-privacy-policy-describes-how: This Privacy Policy describes how NJJ Document Services, Inc. d/b/a The Comp Desk ("The Comp Desk," "we," "our," or "us") collects, uses, shares, and protects information when you use thecompdesk.com, our mobile and browser-extension applications, our calculators, our attorney-referral and contact forms, and registered attorney accounts (collectively, the "Services").
privacy.the-services-are-operated-by: The Services are operated by NJJ Document Services, Inc., a company doing business as The Comp Desk. We are responsible for the personal information processed through the Services as described in this policy.
privacy.this-policy-covers-the-thecompdesk: This policy covers the thecompdesk.com website, our mobile app and browser extension, our workers' compensation calculators, our contact and attorney-referral forms, our reminder features, and registered attorney accounts. It does not cover the practices of independent attorneys to whom you may be referred, who maintain their own privacy practices and become responsible for your information once it is shared with them.
privacy.this-policy-applies-to-injured: This policy applies to injured workers who use our tools or request a referral, participating attorneys who hold accounts with us, and general visitors to our site.
privacy.our-calculators-run-entirely-in: Our calculators run entirely in your browser; the wages, dates, and other figures you enter are processed on your device and are not transmitted to or stored on our servers. Separately, if you submit a contact form, request an attorney referral, create an account, or opt in to IME or hearing reminders, we collect the information you choose to provide. Depending on what you do, this may include your name, email address, phone number, and details about your potential workers' compensation matter, so that we can respond to you, route your request to a participating attorney, or send the reminders you requested.
privacy.if-you-register-as-a: If you register as a participating attorney, we collect your account email, name, firm, professional and verification details, and your subscription and payment status.
privacy.when-you-visit-the-services: When you visit the Services we automatically collect limited technical information such as browser type, operating system, device and screen characteristics, language preference, and the referring URL. This information is collected through privacy-respecting analytics that strip personal identifiers and anonymize IP addresses before data is recorded.
privacy.we-obtain-public-professional-directory: We obtain public professional-directory information (for example, from the National Provider Identifier registry) to build and maintain our directory of workers' compensation providers. We also receive confirmation of payment and subscription status from our payment processors; we do not collect or store your full payment-card details.
privacy.2-5-road-to-recovery: 2.5 Road to Recovery personalization and Comp Buddy AI features (optional)
privacy.if-you-choose-to-personalize: If you choose to personalize your Road to Recovery, we ask a short questionnaire about your work injury — such as when it happened, whether you told your employer and filed a claim, which body parts were affected, surgery and work status, your age range, and whether you already have an attorney. Your answers are stored with your account under strict access controls, are visible only to you, and are used solely to personalize your own roadmap and checklist. Completing the questionnaire requires your express consent, and you can update or redo your answers at any time. Similarly, if you use the Comp Buddy assistant, the messages you send and any document photos you attach are used to generate a reply; we log only usage metadata (not your message text or images) on our servers.
privacy.3-1-delivering-the-referral: 3.1 Delivering the referral and lead-distribution service
privacy.we-use-the-information-you: We use the information you submit through a referral or contact form to evaluate your request and route it to one or more participating attorneys who may be able to assist with your potential claim.
privacy.we-use-account-information-to: We use account information to authenticate registered attorneys, save their work, and administer subscriptions.
privacy.if-you-provide-a-phone: If you provide a phone number to The Comp Desk — by submitting our contact form, signing up for an account, requesting an attorney referral, opting in to IME reminders, or contacting our support number — you consent to receive transactional and customer-care SMS messages from us at that number. Message frequency varies based on your activity. Message and data rates may apply. You can opt out at any time by replying STOP to any message; you can request help by replying HELP. We do not sell, share, or transfer your phone number or SMS opt-in data to third parties for marketing purposes. SMS opt-in consent is not a condition of using The Comp Desk's services or receiving an attorney referral.
privacy.we-use-aggregate-de-identified: We use aggregate, de-identified usage data to understand how the Services are used and to improve them.
privacy.we-use-information-as-needed: We use information as needed to comply with applicable law, enforce our terms, prevent fraud or abuse, and protect the rights and safety of our users and the public.
privacy.to-personalize-your-road-to: To personalize your Road to Recovery, our software applies fixed rules to your questionnaire answers on your device and in our systems. The plain-English explanations shown on personalized roadmaps are generated with the help of an AI service (Anthropic) — but from a de-identified case profile only (for example, "arm or shoulder injury, out of work, age band, at maximum medical improvement"). Your name, contact details, dates, and free-text answers are never included in that generation, and the resulting explanations are general educational templates shared by everyone with a similar profile — they are never advice about your specific case. Comp Buddy assistant conversations are likewise processed by the same AI service to generate replies. Our AI provider processes this data to provide the service and does not use it to train its models.
privacy.3-7-optional-opt-in: 3.7 Optional, opt-in research use (off by default)
privacy.separately-from-personalization-we-ask: Separately from personalization, we ask whether we may use anonymized patterns from your case to improve guidance for other workers. This choice is optional, is off by default, and does not affect your access to any feature. If you opt in, we use only aggregated, de-identified information (never your name, contact details, or any detail that could identify you), reviewed in groups rather than individually. You can change this choice at any time by updating your questionnaire answers or emailing privacy@thecompdesk.com.
privacy.when-you-request-a-referral: When you request a referral, we share the contact and matter information you submit with the participating attorney or attorneys we route you to, so they can evaluate and contact you about your potential claim. Those attorneys then handle your information under their own privacy practices.
privacy.we-rely-on-trusted-service: We rely on trusted service providers who process information only to provide services to us, including website hosting (Vercel), authentication and database services (Supabase), email delivery (Resend), telephone and SMS messaging (OpenPhone), payment processing (Stripe, and Apple or Google for in-app purchases), artificial-intelligence processing for the Comp Buddy assistant and personalized roadmap explanations (Anthropic — which does not use this data to train its models), and privacy-respecting analytics. These providers are bound by their own privacy and security obligations.
privacy.we-may-disclose-information-if: We may disclose information if required by law, subpoena, or other legal process, or where we believe disclosure is necessary to protect our rights, your safety, or the safety of others.
privacy.if-we-are-involved-in: If we are involved in a merger, acquisition, financing, or sale of assets, information may be transferred as part of that transaction, subject to this policy.
privacy.4-5-what-we-do: 4.5 What we do not share or sell
privacy.we-do-not-sell-your: We do not sell your personal information. We do not use advertising cookies, tracking pixels, or third-party ad networks, and we do not share your information with advertisers. In particular, we do not sell, share, or transfer your phone number or SMS opt-in data to third parties for marketing purposes.
privacy.you-may-request-access-to: You may request access to or correction of the personal information we hold about you by emailing privacy@thecompdesk.com. We will respond within 30 days.
privacy.if-you-have-an-account: If you have an account, you may request deletion at any time using the account-deletion feature or by emailing privacy@thecompdesk.com.
privacy.you-can-opt-out-of: You can opt out of SMS messages at any time by replying STOP to any message, and you can unsubscribe from marketing emails using the link in those emails. Opting out of transactional messages may affect features you have requested, such as reminders.
privacy.depending-on-where-you-live: Depending on where you live, you may have additional rights under applicable state privacy law. Residents of New York and California, among others, may have rights to access, correct, delete, or restrict certain processing of their personal information. To exercise these rights, contact privacy@thecompdesk.com.
privacy.you-can-update-or-redo: You can update or redo your Road to Recovery questionnaire at any time from the roadmap screen ("Update my answers"), which also lets you change your anonymized-research choice. Deleting your account deletes your questionnaire answers and personalized roadmap data. You can also make either request by emailing privacy@thecompdesk.com.
privacy.we-use-administrative-technical-and: We use administrative, technical, and organizational safeguards designed to protect personal information against unauthorized access, loss, or misuse. No method of transmission or storage is completely secure, and we cannot guarantee absolute security.
privacy.we-retain-aggregate-analytics-data: We retain aggregate analytics data for up to 24 months. Account data is retained while your account is active. Road to Recovery questionnaire answers and checklist progress are retained while your account is active and are deleted when your account is deleted; the general, de-identified roadmap explanations described in Section 3.6 contain no personal information and may be retained. Information you submit through a referral or contact form is retained as long as needed to provide the service you requested and as required by law, after which it is deleted or de-identified.
privacy.if-a-data-breach-affecting: If a data breach affecting your personal information occurs, we will notify affected users and applicable authorities as required by law.
privacy.we-use-a-small-number: We use a small number of first-party cookies and local-storage items necessary to operate the Services and remember your preferences, such as recording when you have dismissed our analytics notice. These do not contain personal information.
privacy.we-use-privacy-respecting-analytics: We use privacy-respecting analytics (Vercel Web Analytics) configured to strip personal identifiers and anonymize IP addresses. We do not use session recording, heatmaps, or advertising trackers.
privacy.we-honor-browser-do-not: We honor browser "Do Not Track" signals where technically feasible.
privacy.the-services-are-intended-for: The Services are intended for adults and are not directed to children under the age of 13. We do not knowingly collect personal information from anyone under 13. If you believe a child has provided us with personal information, please contact privacy@thecompdesk.com and we will promptly delete it.
privacy.we-may-update-this-privacy: We may update this Privacy Policy from time to time. Changes will be posted to this page with an updated "Last updated" date. For material changes, we will make reasonable efforts to notify registered users by email. Continued use of the Services after changes take effect constitutes acceptance of the revised policy.

extension-privacy.the-comp-desk-browser-extension: The Comp Desk browser extension ("the extension") is published by NJJ Document Services, Inc. This page explains what data the extension collects, why, and how long we keep it. If anything here is unclear, email contact@thecompdesk.com.
extension-privacy.highlighted-text-you-choose-to: Highlighted text you choose to send. Only text you explicitly select and submit (via the right-click menu or the side panel composer) is transmitted to our servers. The extension does not read, scrape, or monitor pages you do not act on.
extension-privacy.chat-content-and-tool-inputs: Chat content and tool inputs/outputs. Your messages, the calculator inputs the model extracts from them, and the calculator results are sent to our server-side function so Claude can respond.
extension-privacy.authentication-token-if-you-sign: Authentication token. If you sign in, a Supabase session token is stored in the extension's local storage (chrome.storage.local) so you stay signed in. Anonymous use is supported — no sign-in required for free calculators.
extension-privacy.ip-address-transient-used-by: IP address (transient). Used by our edge function for rate limiting on anonymous use only. Bucketed by 24-hour windows; not persisted beyond that.
extension-privacy.the-contents-of-any-page: The contents of any page you visit, beyond text you explicitly highlight and send.
extension-privacy.form-data-passwords-or-cookies: Form data, passwords, or cookies from third-party sites.
extension-privacy.any-data-from-pages-where: Any data from pages where you do not invoke the extension.
extension-privacy.to-run-nys-workers-compensation: To run NYS Workers' Compensation calculations and return them to you.
extension-privacy.to-track-per-session-inference: To track per-session inference cost so we can stay within budget.
extension-privacy.to-enforce-tier-based-access: To enforce tier-based access (Free vs. Pro vs. Firm) and rate limits.
extension-privacy.chat-sessions-are-stored-in: Chat sessions are stored in our advisor_sessions table for up to 90 days for cost reconciliation and quality review, then purged. You may request earlier deletion at any time by emailing contact@thecompdesk.com.
extension-privacy.cloudflare-request-transit-used-by: Cloudflare — request transit (used by Supabase edge functions).
extension-privacy.no-advertising-marketing-or-analytics: No advertising, marketing, or analytics third parties.
extension-privacy.activetab-read-the-text-you: activeTab — read the text you've selected when you click the context menu. Scoped to the active tab only, only when you invoke the extension.
extension-privacy.contextmenus-register-the-calculate-with: contextMenus — register the "Calculate with The Comp Desk" right-click entry.
extension-privacy.storage-store-your-session-token: storage — store your session token and chat history locally.
extension-privacy.identity-handle-google-oauth-sign: identity — handle Google OAuth sign-in via Chrome's built-in flow.
extension-privacy.the-extension-does-not-request: The extension does not request broad host permissions (no <all_urls> in host_permissions). It cannot read any page until you explicitly highlight text and invoke it.
extension-privacy.you-can-sign-out-and: You can sign out and clear extension storage at any time via Chrome's extension settings. To request deletion of stored chat history, email contact@thecompdesk.com.
extension-privacy.the-extension-is-a-document: The extension is a document preparation and information service operated by NJJ Document Services, Inc. It is not legal advice and does not create an attorney-client relationship.
extension-privacy.we-will-update-this-page: We will update this page when our practices change. The "Last updated" date at the top reflects the most recent revision.
extension-privacy.for-questions-contact-njj-document: For questions, contact NJJ Document Services, Inc. at contact@thecompdesk.com.
